checks: Verified that the only decoded field change is the explicit mixed-integer maximization domain in the statement, with identical proof bytes. The symmetric submeasure gives a depth at a point in that domain. The integer census, raised q threshold and p isolator prove the exact bound and strict uniqueness across the full domain.
Verified source 1d1be0b22c707856 §§6 and 8, (12), and the base construction in §7 against the exact source digest.

The lattice-preserving coordinate flip gives q=0 and p=−1_I. A coordinate −1 in the convex hull forces every base generator in the representation to be p. The original vertex fibers remain K because all continuous generators are in K. The hull includes the full product [0,1]^n × K.

Reflection through (q,g) swaps p and v and swaps the retained A and 2g−A, while preserving the central K and each fiber volume. Because 2g−A⊆K, this is an actual submeasure of mass V+2a. Opposite closed through-point halfspaces cover the ambient space and have equal retained mass, so each gets at least V/2+a even if a whole fiber lies on the boundary.

Independently expanded δ_w(p) as 2(k+1)j+(k+1)s−(k−j) and checked all 86,368 pairs of nonempty I and nonzero w for n=1,…,8. With j+s≥1 the all-dimensional lower bound is one. At q, δ_q(p)=−k and δ_q is at least one at every other cube vertex.

Every chosen nonzero continuous direction has nontrivial range on full-dimensional K. Symmetry makes its normalized midpoint value 1/2; opposite traces cover K and each has half the volume because their common boundary is null. The base penalties isolate each canonical fiber cap, with the q bonus retaining all of A.

For y≠g at q, choose the direction y−g. The raised normalized threshold lies in (1/2,1], and an open slab between the central and raised levels meets a neighborhood of g inside K in positive volume. This lowers the own cap strictly while preserving the endpoint traces. Other cube points pay at most V/2 and p pays a via a vertical cap. This covers boundary points, d=1, n=1 and a=V.

There are exactly 2^n K-fibers and the one A-fiber. Hence the denominator is 2^nV+a and division gives the stated normalized value. In d=1 full-dimensional compact convex K is an interval, and the proof applies to every contained positive interval.

overlap.comparison: For one reflected pair with middle and far fibers K and near fiber A, its midpoint compatibility follows from A⊆K and convexity. At g, A∩(2g−K)=A and D_K(g)=V/2, so it already implies the exact lower certificate V/2+a. Its result gives no isolating upper cover, binary census, or strict uniqueness.

Its structured box example also bounds mixed depth by half the centrally symmetric overlap mass. Its tree support and lower-bound conclusion differ from the binary-core exact maximum and uniqueness here.

initial_review.readability: The reflected submeasure uses full A at p and only its reflection at v. Both bodies can be retained even when a=V. The opposite chosen directions provide the cover, and strict reduction at a noncentral q point uses its own chosen direction.
initial_review.summary: Central symmetry gives the exact all-direction lower bound at (q,g), and the lifted finite caps prove the matching value and strict uniqueness without a smallness threshold beyond containment.
